newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists say militant threat exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists say militant threat exaggerated.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islam-based Welfare Party said on Friday that the secularist elite, led by the powerful generals, was exaggerating the threat from Moslem radicals in a campaign by the army against religious activism.
"I believe it is not correct to say that the vast majority of the nation constitutes a potential threat," Welfare Party spokesman Suleyman Arif Emre told a news conference.
"There are badly educated groups in every country," he said. "The way to deal with them is through education."
The powerful army told a news briefing this week that it regards a proposed anti-Islamist crackdown as a matter of life and death for Turkey, overwhelmingly Moslem but officially secular.
But the Islamist-led government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has stalled on complying with a series of tough measures against Islamists ordered by the army.
Emre said a military plan that would close religious high schools, known as Imam Hatips, would close off a legal channel for Islamist sentiment and encourage militants.
"You talk about the fundamentalist threat at briefings and then try to close down the antidote to that, the Imam Hatips. You are diagnosing an illness and then banning the medicine."
Welfare leader Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, arrived at an air base at the northern town of Merzifon for an air force ceremony, Anatolian news agency said.
The ceremony was also to be attended by armed forces chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi, it said.
